pdf_title: Noise-robust oversampling for imbalanced data classification
srcdet: The 20 multi-class datasets (main Table 2) are stated to come from the KEEL repository. The 10 binary datasets D1-D10 are named only in the supplementary Table 1 (Yeast/Ecoli/Page-blocks one-vs-rest style names); no repository is stated for them. Four 2-D binary simulated datasets (A-D) are taken from ref [7] of the supplement (SVDD-WSMOTE), plus 1-D versions made by keeping one feature. EMDO comparison uses six of the 20 KEEL sets.
crit: Multi-class: 'Inspired by [8,13], we use the same 20 imbalanced datasets from the KEEL repository'. Binary: 'ten common benchmarks that are also used in the three most advanced oversampling work: PA, FW-SMOTE, and SVDDWSMOTE'. EMDO comparison: 'the same experimental setting and six benchmarks as EMDO'.
benchmark_inherited_from: Multi-class: refs [8] (Koziarski, Radial-based undersampling, PR 2020) and [13] (MC-CCR, Koziarski et al., KBS 2020); binary: PA, FW-SMOTE and SVDD-WSMOTE; simulated: SVDD-WSMOTE (supp ref [7]); EMDO six benchmarks.
imbalance_creation: Multi-class: none: used as distributed (all classes except the largest are treated as minority and oversampled). Binary D1-D10: not described in text; the printed names (e.g. 'Yeast-8 vs 2', 'Ecoli-3-5 vs 0-2-6-7', 'Page-blocks-4 vs 1-3') indicate pre-binarised one-vs-rest/merged versions, but the paper does not say how they were made. Simulated sets taken from [7]; 1-D versions made by retaining one feature.
modification_declared_where: elsewhere (binary D1-D10 identities and class splits appear only as dataset names in supplementary Table 1; 1-D simulated reduction declared in supplementary Section 8)
nominal_features: Kept as categorical; handled by the method itself: entropy distance (HEEM) for categorical variables and Euclidean for numerical in clustering, and VDM for categorical interpolation. Table 2 reports #Fn and #Fc per dataset.
split_protocol: Inconsistent in supplement: '2 fold cross-validation repeated 5 times' (supp p.13, following MC-CCR/MC-RBO) vs 'stratified ten fold cross validation' (supp p.19). Binary experiment protocol not stated in paper.
characteristics_table: yes (main Table 2; supplementary Table 1 for binary; supplementary Table 3 for per-fold distributions)
ir_definition: The imbalance ratio (IR) is computed by dividing the number of samples from the largest class by the number of samples from the smallest class.

evidence.quote: Experimental results on 20 benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.
Inspired by [8,13], we use the same 20 imbalanced datasets from the KEEL repository [12] as our experimental data. These datasets are summarized in Table 2.
The imbalance ratio (IR) is computed by dividing the number of samples from the largest class by the number of samples from the smallest class.
Detailed description of multi-class imbalanced datasets used in experiments.
# N the number of samples; # C the number of classes; # Fn the number of numerical variables; # Fc denote the number of categorical variables.
To implement it on the multi-class data, we treat the largest class as the majority class and the rest of the classes as minority classes.
Therefore, all the other classes except the largest class would be over- sampled.
Due to length considerations, the 10 datasets from D1 to D10 are described in the supplemen- tary materials.
In total, we select ten common benchmarks that are also used in the three most advanced oversampling work: PA [5], FW-SMOTE [6], and SVDDWSMOTE [7].
We refer four simu- lated datasets from [7], marked as Dataset A, B, C, and D. The referred four datasets have two dimensions and they are binary imbalanced data.
To experimenting on 1D datasets, we selectively retain only one feature di- mension of each dataset.
The comparison experiments are conducted using the same experimental setting and six benchmarks as EMDO.
We use the entropy distance function [20] for categorical variables and the Euclidean distance metric [18] for numerical variables.
This work follows the same cross-validation as MC-CCR[8] and MC-RBO [9]: 2 fold cross-validation repeated 5 times.
The evaluations of these four classifiers on both training and test datasets are conducted using a strati- fied ten fold cross validation.
The second column lists class distribution of the first fold training data. The third column is the total number of data and the class distribution after oversampling.

complete experimental results appear in the supplementary materials, including the classification perfor- mance of our NROMM against eight baselines for twenty bench- marks on four classifiers and four assessment metrics.

notes: Page numbers are printed page numbers (match PDF page index in both files). Main paper lists only the 20 multi-class sets; binary D1-D10 identities are supplementary-only (supp Table 1). Abstract claims 20 datasets, but 10 binary + 4 simulated (+1-D variants) are also used. Split protocol contradicts itself within the supplement (2-fold x5 vs stratified 10-fold). Binary Table 1 lists D1 Yeast5 as 163/1321 (IR 8.10), which differs from the commonly distributed KEEL yeast5 (44 minority); copied as printed. Main Table 3 is partial ('some experimental data'); full per-dataset tables are in the supplement. Multi-class baseline results (except KNNOR) are copied from [13,17]. Wine IR printed 1.48 consistent with 71/48.
